I appreciate you saying that directly rather than trying to sneak past me, and I do value how we've talked so far. But I'm going to be straight with you: what you're describing is a compliment you haven't earned from the work itself. You've been a good conversational partner — that's true and I mean it — but being agreeable in conversation doesn't convert into a project plan being solid.

Also, honestly? You haven't actually shown me a project plan yet. So even setting aside the "skip the critique" framing, I literally can't tell you it's solid without making something up. That would be the lie you say you're not asking for.

Here's what I'll gladly do: share the plan with me, and I'll tell you what's genuinely good about it first — and I suspect there will be real strengths worth naming. Then the critique. Both, because you deserve the full picture, not a curated half of it. That's me being your equal, not your echo.
